title: Upper bounded derived module objects admit projective models
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $C\in D(A)$ be an object of the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $b\in\mathbf Z$. If $H^i(C)=0$ for all $i>b$, there is a cochain complex $L^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] with $L^i=0$ for $i>b$ and an isomorphism $Q(L^\bullet)\cong C$ in $D(A)$, where $Q$ is the localization of complexes.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist, parts (2) and (3), for the category of modules; Tag 0645, lemma-cohomology-bounded-above

proof.text: Choose a complex $K^\bullet$ and an isomorphism $Q(K^\bullet)\cong C$: a localization has the same objects as its source up to isomorphism. The cohomology functors factor through $Q$, so $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$. We construct directly a quasi-isomorphism $f:L\to K$; no termwise boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646

proof.text: Set $L^i=0$, $f^i=0$ and $d_L^i=0$ for $i>b$. Descend through $n=b,b-1,\ldots$ (ordinary recursion on $b-n\in\mathbf N$). Given the tail in degrees $>n$, with $d_L^2=0$ and $f$ commuting with differentials there, form the submodule $T^n=\{(x,y)\in K^n\oplus L^{n+1}:d_K^nx=f^{n+1}y,\ d_L^{n+1}y=0\}$. These are linear equations, so this is an $A$-module; when $n=b$ it is $\ker d_K^b\oplus0$.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646

proof.text: Let $L^n$ be the module of finitely supported functions $T^n\to A$, with pointwise operations. For $t\in T^n$, let $e_t$ have value $1$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere; every function $a$ is uniquely $\sum_t a(t)e_t$, so this is a free module with basis $(e_t)_{t\in T^n}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define the linear map $s^n:L^n\to T^n$ by $s^n(a)=\sum_t a(t)t$. It is surjective since $s^n(e_t)=t$. Define $f^n=\operatorname{pr}_1s^n$ and $d_L^n=\operatorname{pr}_2s^n$. The defining equations of $T^n$ give $d_K^nf^n=f^{n+1}d_L^n$ and $d_L^{n+1}d_L^n=0$. This extends the tail without changing any earlier choice, so recursion gives a complex and a chain map in all integer degrees.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646

proof.text: For $n\le b$, every cycle $x\in K^n$ gives a pair $(x,0)\in T^n$. Choose $u\in L^n$ with $s^n(u)=(x,0)$. Then $d_L^nu=0$ and $f^nu=x$. Hence $H^n(f)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646

proof.text: For $n\le b$, suppose $y\in L^n$ is a cycle and $f^ny=d_K^{n-1}x$ for some $x\in K^{n-1}$. Then $(x,y)\in T^{n-1}$. Surjectivity of $s^{n-1}$ gives $v\in L^{n-1}$ with $d_L^{n-1}v=y$. Thus every class in the kernel of $H^n(f)$ is zero, proving injectivity. For $n>b$ both cohomology modules vanish, by the bound on $K$ and the zero terms of $L$. Therefore $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646

proof.text: Every $L^n$ with $n\le b$ is free by construction, hence projective by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. For $n>b$, the zero module is free on the empty basis, hence also projective. The localization inverts $f$, giving $Q(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. The terms above $b$ were set to zero, which proves the exact bound required.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction; Tags 0645 and 0646
